Lena (AE): Quick ask — Oakmont Bank POC: must BYO-CMK across CloudHSM and an on-prem HSM with quarterly rotations and proof of non-export. They also want cost delta vs standard hosted. Can we reply today?
Diego (Solutions Eng): We support hybrid BYO. Two modes: proxy connector (fast) or direct peering (lower latency). Key point: avoid per-token HSM calls by caching DEKs.
Ravi (Crypto Ops): Architecture note: master CMKs stay in customer HSMs. Runtime flow: Redwood requests unwrap via mTLS to customer HSM; we cache derived DEKs per session (configurable TTL). Recommended rotation cadence: master rotate window monthly (or as customer requests); ephemeral keys can be sub-24h.
Sophie (Security): For questionnaire: we provide HSM attestation bundle, network allowlist, audit log samples, and a diagram showing we never persist master plaintext. Suggested answer for custody: "Master keys are generated and retained in customer-controlled HSMs; Redwood performs cryptographic ops over authenticated channels and does not store master key material."
Ravi (Crypto Ops): Pricing sketch (ballpark): onboarding fee $6k, monthly connector fee $1,000, per-HSM-op metered $0.018/op (reserved tier lowers to ~$0.005/op). Proxy-mode with DEK cache typically reduces op count to billing-effective level.
Alina (Legal): Standard stance: we do not escrow keys. Any escrow/exception requires signed SOW and legal approval. I'll prepare a one-paragraph addendum if they press.
Diego (Solutions Eng): POC test plan to propose: 24h run, 200k key ops, simulate HSM downtime 15m, rotation dry-run. We'll log p95 latency.
OncallBot: Ticket created SLS-9902 "oak-hsm-poc" assigned to @Ravi.
Lena (AE): Great — I'll forward these bullets to Oakmont procurement. Ping if they ask for FIPS/FedRAMP vendor docs.
Sophie (Security): If they need FIPS 140-3 evidence, ask for HSM vendor certs; we'll bundle them with our connector SBOM.
